name: DialogueRunner
src_typeComment: Plug-and-play dialogue tree runner: assign UI references, call StartDialogue(rootNode). Reuses EXISTING toolkit pieces instead of duplicating them — TMPTypewriterEffect for the per-character text reveal, Blackboard for optional conditional choices (e.g. only offer "Ask about the key" once a quest flag is set) — neither is required, both are optional and null-checked throughout.

src_serialized.name: blackboard
src_serialized.tooltip: Optional — gates DialogueChoice.requiredBlackboardKey checks. Leave unassigned if you don't use conditional choices.

src_serialized.name: typewriter
src_serialized.tooltip: Optional — if assigned, dialogue text reveals character-by-character instead of appearing instantly.

src_serialized.name: choiceButtonPrefab
src_serialized.tooltip: A template Button (kept inactive in the scene) cloned once per available choice, then destroyed and rebuilt on the next node.

src_members.sig: public bool IsActive { get; private set; }
src_members.name: IsActive
Advance
src_members.comment: Advances a no-choice node. Does nothing if the current node HAS choices (use SelectChoice instead). The classic dialogue-UI convention: if the typewriter is still revealing, the first Advance() completes the line instantly instead of skipping straight to the next node.

src_members.name: GetAvailableChoices
src_members.comment: Public rather than just an internal filtering step — a custom dialogue UI (not using the built-in choiceButtonPrefab cloning below) can call this directly to know what to render.
